titleEn: I Am the Big Girl—I Can Help!

pages.text: "Mom, look at me!" Riri in her yellow hat raised both arms by the row of shells. But Mom was holding and patting the neighbor's baby rabbit, in her care for the day. "Shh, the baby is sleeping. A little quieter." Riri slowly lowered her arms.

"When the baby sleeps, will you play with me?" Riri held the blue apron. "Of course. Wait a little, please," Mom answered, holding the baby. Riri hugged her knees by the stove. Outside, the gray winter sea rolled.

The baby opened its eyes and wailed. Mom was warming porridge in the kitchen. "Do not cry. This big girl will choose the nicest thing for you." Riri searched the box. Shells, one, two; pebbles, one, two—choosing took a long time.
Meanwhile, the crying grew louder. Even when Riri offered shells or pebbles, the baby shook its head. Not knowing what to do, Riri squeezed her hands together.
Mom returned with the porridge bowl. "Riri, first can you see why the baby is crying?" Riri studied its face. The baby kept reaching its little hands into the air.
"Oh... is there nothing to hold?" Riri touched one finger to its hand. The baby gripped the finger tightly and stopped crying! "Mom, the baby stopped! I am the big girl—I can help!"
The baby smiled at Riri. Her heart fluttered. "Peekaboo!" made it giggle; a song made its feet bounce. Her sulky feelings melted away.
"Mom, this time I will sing a lullaby." Riri sang softly. An empty porridge bowl sat nearby. The baby slowly closed its eyes.
Riri sat with her knees up beside the sleeping baby. "One, first see why the baby is crying! Two, give one finger to hold! Three, sing a lullaby!" It was warm and quiet by the stove.

Mom drew Riri onto her lap and hugged her tightly. "Our Riri is such a lovely big girl." There were things she could do for a little baby. Watching it sleep, Riri whispered, "I am the big girl—I can help!"
